name: Olive and fig horticulture in the Jordan Valley
summary: At Chalcolithic Tel Tsaf, charred olive wood and young fig branches point to fruit-tree cultivation about 7,000 years ago.
description: Charcoal from the Chalcolithic village of Tel Tsaf in the Central Jordan Valley, Israel, includes abundant olive wood, although the site lies outside the wild olive's natural range, and young fig branches that probably come from pruning. The authors take this as olive and fig horticulture practised as early as 7,000 years ago and call it one of the earliest examples of fruit tree cultivation worldwide.

impact.note: Tree crops that bear for decades and give storable oil and dried fruit were a new capability (depth 2) with a few successors such as oil pressing (generativity 1); reach is 1 because the Mediterranean olive economy is not shown to descend from this Jordan Valley community rather than from other Levantine centres.

date.label: c. 7000 years ago (c. 5050 BCE)
date.basis: The approximate chronology of the two-species interpretation follows Langgut and Garfinkel (2022). Langgut (2024), Table 2, reports 7160–6950 cal BP for an olive branch and repeats 6960–6860 cal BP for a fig twig at 68.2% probability.

events.statement: Olive charcoal and young fig branches from Tel Tsaf are interpreted as evidence of local fruit-tree cultivation about 7000 years ago. Direct radiocarbon dates from Area C include a young olive branch and a fig twig.

evidence.supports: olive ( Olea europaea ) and fig ( Ficus carica ) horticulture was practiced as early as 7000 years ago in the Central Jordan Valley, Israel
Adds a direct 7160–6950 cal BP assay on the young olive branch Beta-657404. The fig twig Beta-585311 date was previously reported.

date.label: 7200-6700 cal BP (c. 5250-4750 BCE)
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: The charcoal assemblage on which the finding rests comes from the Chalcolithic site of Tel Tsaf, occupied 7200-6700 calibrated years before present, about 5250-4750 BCE.

evidence.supports: It is based on the anatomical identification of a charcoal assemblage recovered from the Chalcolithic (7200–6700 cal. BP) site of Tel Tsaf.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Grapevine and date palm cultivation, which this source does not cover.
The Gilgal fig claim c. 9400 BCE and the date of the first grafting.
Whether Mediterranean olive growing descends from the southern Levant or from other centres.
Langgut (2024) proposes earlier cultivation on the Carmel coast and in the Galilee. The excavated evidence leaves the origin and route of the olive trees at Tel Tsaf open.

evidence.supports: Regional archaeological and pollen comparisons motivate a transfer hypothesis without identifying its route or specific source.

research.note: The source calls Tel Tsaf one of the earliest examples of fruit tree cultivation, not the first known, and does not say how the practice reached the site.
